source.title: Open Problems in the Function Theory of the Bergman Space

accepted.question_text: Let D be the open unit disk and let L2_a(D) be the Bergman space of square-area-integrable analytic functions on D with normalized area measure dS = dxdy/pi. A closed subspace J of L2_a(D) is invariant if zf belongs to J whenever f belongs to J, where z(lambda) = lambda is the coordinate function. How can one characterize all invariant subspaces of L2_a(D)?
accepted.context_brief: Invariant subspaces of the Bergman space

evidence.quote: A closed subspace J of L2_a(D) is said to be z-invariant, or simply invariant, provided the product zf belongs to J whenever f ∈ J.
Problem 1.1. Characterize the invariant subspaces of L2_a(D).

accepted.question_text: Let D be the open unit disk and let L2_a(D) be the Bergman space of square-area-integrable analytic functions on D. A sequence A = {a_j} of points in D is an L2_a(D) zero sequence if there is a function in L2_a(D) whose zeros are precisely A, counted with multiplicity. Which sequences A in D are exactly the zero sequences of L2_a(D)?
accepted.context_brief: Zero sequences in the Bergman space

evidence.quote: A sequence A = {aj}j of points in D, is said to be an L2_a(D) zero sequence if there exists a function in L2_a(D) that vanishes precisely on the sequence A, counting multiplicities.
Problem 1.2. Characterize the L2_a(D) zero sequences.

accepted.question_text: For an inner divisor G of L2_a(D), let Phi_G be the Green-potential function associated with |G|^2 - 1. Theorem 1.6 gives the isometry ||Gf||^2_L2 = ||f||^2_L2 + integral_D |f'(z)|^2 Phi_G(z) dS(z) for all f in the Hardy space H2(D). Does this isometry extend to every f in L2_a(D)? If it does not always extend, for exactly which inner divisors G does the extension hold?

evidence.quote: Theorem 1.6. If G is an inner divisor for L2_a(D), then the function Phi_G meets 0 ≤ Phi_G(z) ≤ 1 - |z|2, z ∈ D, and we have the isometry ... valid for all f ∈ H2(D).
Problem 1.7. Does the isometry in Theorem 1.6 extend to all f ∈ L2_a(D)? If not, then for which inner divisors G is this so?

accepted.question_text: For zero sequences A and B in L2_a(D), let G_A and G_B denote their associated zero divisors. Define G ≺ H to mean ||Gf||_L2 ≤ ||Hf||_L2 for every bounded analytic function f in H∞(D). If A is contained in B as zero sequences, must the domination relation G_A ≺ G_B hold?

evidence.quote: The precise definition of G ≺ H, for G, H ∈ L2_a(D), is ||Gf||_L2 ≤ ||Hf||_L2, f ∈ H∞(D).
Conjecture 2.1. If A, B are two zero sequences for L2_a(D) having A ⊂ B, then G_A ≺ G_B.

accepted.question_text: For finite zero sequences A and B in L2_a(D), let Phi_A and Phi_B be the Green-potential functions associated with the zero divisors G_A and G_B. If A is contained in B, is Phi_A(z) ≤ Phi_B(z) for every z in D?

evidence.quote: We write here Phi_A instead of Phi_GA, for a given zero sequence A.
Conjecture 2.2. If A, B are two finite zero sequences for L2_a(D) having A ⊂ B, then Phi_A ≤ Phi_B holds on D.

accepted.question_text: For every finite zero divisor G of the Bergman space L2_a(D), is the Green function for the singular fourth-order elliptic operator Delta |G|^{-2} Delta positive on D x D, where the Green function U_G(z, zeta) solves Delta_z |G(z)|^{-2} Delta_z U_G(z, zeta) = delta_zeta(z) in D with U_G and its boundary gradient equal to zero on the unit circle?
accepted.context_brief: Positivity of a singular fourth-order Green function

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.1. The Green function for the singular fourth order elliptic operator Delta |G|^{-2} Delta is positive on D x D for every finite zero divisor G for the space L2_a(D).
Here we mean by the Green function the solution U_G(z, zeta) to the problem Delta_z |G(z)|^{-2} Delta_z U_G(z, zeta) = delta_zeta(z), z ∈ D.

accepted.question_text: For the weighted biharmonic operator Delta (1 - |z|^2)^{-alpha} Delta on the unit disk D, is its Green function U_alpha(z, zeta) positive on D x D for every real parameter alpha with -1 < alpha ≤ 1?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.3. The Green function U_alpha(z, zeta) for the weighted biharmonic operator Delta (1 - |z|2)^{-alpha} Delta is positive on D x D for all real parameter values alpha having -1 < alpha ≤ 1.

accepted.question_text: Let A be a zero sequence for L2_a(D), let G_A be its associated zero divisor, and let I(A) = {f in L2_a(D): f vanishes on A}. Does G_A generate I(A) as an invariant subspace, meaning that the functions G_A, zG_A, z^2G_A, and so on span a dense subspace of I(A)?

evidence.quote: Problem 4.1. Does G_A generate I(A) = {f ∈ L2_a(D) : f = 0 on A} as an invariant subspace? In other words, do the functions G_A, zG_A, z2G_A, ... span a dense subspace of I(A)?

accepted.question_text: For every zero sequence A of L2_a(D), does the quotient G_{A union {0}} / G_A belong to the Smirnov space on D, where the Smirnov space consists of quotients f/g with f and g bounded analytic functions on D and g outer?
accepted.context_brief: Adding a zero to a Bergman zero divisor

evidence.quote: Problem 4.2. Does G_{A∪{0}}/G_A always belong to the Smirnov space on D? The Smirnov space consists of all quotients f/g, where f, g ∈ H∞(D), and g is an outer function.

accepted.question_text: Let omega be a continuous function on the unit disk D satisfying (1 - |z|^2)^2 ≤ omega(z) ≤ 2(1 - |z|^2). In the weighted Bergman space L2_a(D, omega) of holomorphic functions f with integral_D |f(z)|^2 omega(z) dS(z) finite, must the polynomials be dense? If this is not known under only those bounds, does polynomial density follow after adding the regularity condition Delta^2 omega ≥ 4 on D?
accepted.context_brief: Polynomial density in weighted Bergman spaces

evidence.quote: Problem 4.4. Suppose omega is a continuous function on D satisfying (1 - |z|2)2 ≤ omega(z) ≤ 2(1 - |z|2), z ∈ D.

Must then the polynomials be dense in the weighted Bergman space L2_a(D, omega) of all holomorphic functions in D having integral_D |f(z)|2 omega(z) dS(z) < +∞? What if we make the regularity assumption on omega that Delta2 omega ≥ 4 on D?

accepted.question_text: Is every analytic function f on D satisfying ||f phi||_L2 ≤ ||phi||_H2 for every phi in H2(D) the normal limit of finite zero divisors for the Bergman space?
accepted.context_brief: Carathéodory-type theorem for Bergman zero divisors

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.2. Every analytic function f on D with ||f phi||_L2 ≤ ||phi||_H2, phi ∈ H2(D), is the normal limit of finite zero divisors.

accepted.question_text: Let M(H2, L2_a) be the multiplier space from H2(D) to L2_a(D), with norm ||G|| = sup{||Gf||_L2: f in H2(D), ||f||_H2 ≤ 1}. Is every inner divisor for L2_a(D) approximable by zero divisors in this multiplier norm?
accepted.context_brief: Frostman-type approximation for Bergman inner divisors

evidence.quote: Let M(H2, L2_a) be the space of multipliers H2(D) -> L2_a(D), normed appropriately: ||G|| = sup {||Gf||_L2 : f ∈ H2(D), ||f||_H2 ≤ 1}.
Conjecture 6.2. Every inner divisor for L2_a(D) is approximable by zero divisors in the norm of M(H2, L2_a).

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an absolute constant epsilon with 0 < epsilon < 2^{-1/2} such that, whenever f and g are in L2_a(D) and |f(z)| ≤ |g(z)| throughout the annulus epsilon < |z| < 1, the Bergman L2 norm inequality ||f||_L2 ≤ ||g||_L2 follows?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 7.1. (Korenblum) There exists an absolute constant epsilon, 0 < epsilon < 2^{-1/2}, such that if f, g ∈ L2_a(D) have |f(z)| ≤ |g(z)| in the annulus epsilon < |z| < 1, then ||f||_L2 ≤ ||g||_L2.

accepted.question_text: For f and g in L2_a(D), suppose f ≺ g and g ≺ f, where f ≺ g denotes the Bergman domination relation ||fh||_L2 ≤ ||gh||_L2 for all bounded analytic h. Must f equal gamma g for some unimodular constant gamma? Does the same conclusion hold under the additional assumption that f and g are bounded functions?

evidence.quote: Problem 7.2. Suppose f, g ∈ L2_a(D) have f ≺ g and g ≺ f. Must then f = gamma g for a unimodular constant gamma? What if f and g are bounded functions?
Kehe Zhu has informed me that the answer to Problem 7.2 is affirmative, and in fact a simple consequence of a property of the Berezin transform.

accepted.question_text: A function f in L2_a(D) is cyclic if the functions f, zf, z^2 f, and so on span a dense subspace of L2_a(D). Which functions in L2_a(D) are cyclic?
accepted.context_brief: Cyclic vectors in the Bergman space

evidence.quote: Definition 8.1. A function f ∈ L2_a(D) is cyclic in L2_a(D) if the functions f, zf, z2f, ... span a dense subspace of L2_a(D).
Problem 8.2. Describe the cyclic elements of L2_a(D).

accepted.question_text: Let A^-infty be the algebra of analytic functions on D with polynomial-type boundary growth, meaning |f(z)| ≤ C(f, alpha)(1 - |z|^2)^(-alpha) for some positive alpha and C(f, alpha). It is known that every cyclic element of L2_a(D) generates a dense ideal in A^-infty, equivalently is cyclic in A^-infty. Conversely, if f belongs to L2_a(D) and is cyclic in A^-infty, must f be cyclic in L2_a(D)?

evidence.quote: The space A^-infty consists of all analytic functions f on the unit disk D satisfying the growth condition |f(z)| ≤ C(f, alpha)(1 - |z|2)^(-alpha), z ∈ D.
Problem 8.3. (Korenblum) It is known that every cyclic element of L2_a(D) generates a dense ideal in A^-infty, or in other words, it is cyclic in A^-infty. Does the converse hold?

accepted.question_text: Suppose f belongs to L2_a(D) and satisfies the lower bound |f(z)| ≥ epsilon (1 - |z|^2)^N for every z in D, for some positive constants epsilon and N. Must f be cyclic in L2_a(D)?

evidence.quote: If a function f ∈ L2_a(D) satisfies (8.1) |f(z)| ≥ epsilon (1 - |z|2)^N, z ∈ D, for some positive numbers epsilon, N, then f is invertible in A^-infty.
Problem 8.4. (Shapiro) Suppose f ∈ L2_a(D) satisfies (8.1). Must then f be cyclic in L2_a(D)?

accepted.question_text: For disjoint zero sequences A and B in the unit disk, let I(A) and I(B) be the zero-based invariant subspaces of L2_a(D) consisting of functions vanishing on A and B, respectively. For which pairs of disjoint zero sequences A and B is the algebraic sum I(A) + I(B) dense in L2_a(D)?

evidence.quote: Problem 9.1. Determine for which pairs of disjoint zero sequences A and B the subspace I(A) + I(B) is dense in L2_a(D).

accepted.question_text: Call an invariant subspace I of L2_a(D) maximal if every invariant subspace containing I is either I itself or the whole space L2_a(D). Must every maximal invariant subspace of L2_a(D) have codimension 1?

evidence.quote: Let us agree to say that an invariant subspace I in L2_a(D) is maximal provided every invariant subspace containing it is either I or the whole space L2_a(D).
Problem 10.1. Must every maximal invariant subspace of L2_a(D) have codimension 1?
